newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BARSBY PUTS QUEENSLAND IN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BARSBY PUTS QUEENSLAND IN CHARGE.

text.p: Queensland opener Trevor Barsby hit his first century of the season to transform his side's fortunes against Sheffield Shield leaders Western Australia on Friday.

After Western Australia took a first innings lead of four, Barsby scored 107 to steer Queensland to 195 for two -- 191 ahead with eight wickets in hand -- at the close on the second day of their four-day match at the Gabba in Brisbane.
Western Australia, who lead the competition with 26 points, six points clear of Queensland and New South Wales, scored 183 in their first innings in reply to their opponents' 179.
Jimmy Maher remained unbeaten on 54 in partnership with Australian limited overs international Stuart Law, who was 12 not out.
In Melbourne, New South Wales took a strong grip on their match against Victoria.
At the close on the second day, New South Wales were 114 for two in their second innings, an overall lead of 240, with opener Rodney Davison unbeaten on 48.

New South Wales took a first innings lead of 126 by dismissing Victoria for 164. The home team's position would have even more precarious but for a last wicket partnerhip of 82 between David Saker and Damien Fleming which saved them from following on.
New South Wales all-rounder Brad McNamara claimed five for 30 in 15 overs.
